clue.text: He's unaware that he's making progress

definitions.text: He's unaware that he's making progress

parts.words: He's unaware that he's making progress
parts.note: read as someone oblivious to his own advancement in life, but it means a person literally moving forward on foot while fast asleep

explanation.surface: Someone is getting ahead in life without even noticing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making progress' suggests career success; here it is literal walking, done by someone who is unconscious of it because he is asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who walks in his sleep moves about without any awareness of doing so.

clue.text: Differently worded, but the same thing

definitions.text: Differently worded, but the same thing

parts.words: Differently worded, but the same thing
parts.note: a description of a word that has another spelling and sound yet carries an identical meaning to a second word

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a rephrased statement still says exactly the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A term with a different form but equivalent meaning to another term is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: Always take line to catch fish

indicators.note: to catch means one piece takes the other inside it, as a net holds a fish

parts.note: always means ever, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: An angler's advice: always use a line if you want to land a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' puts L inside EVER, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A young eel is a small fish, often caught migrating up rivers.

clue.text: Fruit, according to Simon, put in muesli first

parts.note: per means according to, as in 'per the instructions'

indicators.note: put in means a letter is placed inside the name Simon

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first signals the opening letter of the word muesli

explanation.surface: A breakfast tip: Simon says the fruit should go into the muesli first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes the opening letter of 'muesli', and 'put in' places it inside the name, making SIMMON; 'according to' is the Latin-derived 'per'.
explanation.definitionFit: The persimmon is an orange fruit from a tree grown in Asia and America, a kind of soft sweet fruit.

clue.text: Sea where Dr zhivago's lover turns up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the name is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Lara is the heroine loved by Yuri Zhivago in Pasternak's novel Doctor Zhivago

explanation.surface: A romantic heroine makes an appearance at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' sounds like arriving; in a down entry it reverses LARA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aral is a largely dried-up inland body of salt water between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.

clue.text: A fine piece of manual work

definitions.text: A fine piece of manual work

parts.words: A fine piece of manual work
parts.note: seems to praise skilled handicraft, but describes a delicate item made to be worn on the hand, manual meaning of the hand

explanation.surface: Praise for a skilled craftsman's handiwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manual' means 'of the hand', and 'fine' means delicate: an item of soft goatskin that covers the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A glove of soft goatskin leather is a fine article of handwear.

clue.text: He's up and moving

parts.note: seems to describe someone just out of bed and active, but means a person seated up on a horse or bike in motion

explanation.surface: Someone has got out of bed and is already on the go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' suggests awake; here it means mounted, as on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A person on horseback is seated high and travels along.

clue.text: Country seats where set teas can be ordered

indicators.note: can be ordered means the letters may be rearranged into a new sequence, as an order is set out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Stately homes offering afternoon set teas to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be ordered' looks like a café menu; it rearranges SETTEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A country seat is a landed family's mansion with its grounds, which is what such properties are.

clue.text: Stop the French raids without help — they're inept!

parts.note: to bung is to stop up or plug a hole
le is French for the

indicators.note: without means a word is removed from the letters of raids

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: French raiders are so clumsy they cannot manage anything unaided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes AID from RAIDS, leaving RS.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy, incompetent people who botch things are exactly what the clue's description means.

clue.text: Don't ever touch on Michael Jackson's ranch!

parts.note: don't ever means never
to touch down is to land, as an aircraft does

explanation.surface: A warning to visitors not to set foot on a pop star's estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Jackson's California estate took its name from Peter Pan's island.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer named his California estate after the fictional island where Peter Pan never grows up.

clue.text: Daughter another relation may discourage

parts.note: an aunt is a further family relative

explanation.surface: A daughter and an aunt might put someone off.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten or intimidate someone is to sap their courage.

clue.text: Scandinavian detectives returning to Norway shortly

parts.note: Nor is the short form of Norway

indicators.note: returning means the word for detectives is read backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detectives

explanation.surface: Police detectives head back to Norway for a brief visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns CID into DIC. CID is Britain's plain-clothes police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the northern European region of Scandinavia and its peoples.

clue.text: Nothing left, but that's fine

definitions.meaning: read cryptically, with nothing on the left side, every bit is on the opposite side
an expression of agreement meaning acceptable or okay

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off running out of everything with cheerful acceptance.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: if nothing is left, everything must be on the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is fine or acceptable is to call it okay; and with nothing on the left, every part is on the opposite side.

clue.text: Notes made on a small manuscript

parts.note: mini means small, as in a miniature

explanation.surface: Someone jots down notes on a little handwritten document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' are musical ones here, not jottings.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a half note, worth two crotchets, is a type of note.

clue.text: The lions sculpted in ancient stones

indicators.note: sculpted means the letters are reshaped into a new form, as stone is carved

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Carved lions found among the remains of an old stone monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sculpted' rearranges THELIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone Age tools and implements are prehistoric worked pieces of rock.

clue.text: Acts as supervisor abroad, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: abroad means in a foreign land across the water

explanation.surface: Someone reportedly manages a team working in a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we're told' signals a sound-alike: the word for abroad is spoken like the word for supervises.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise is to watch over and direct the work of others.

clue.text: Great opera role — got it by working

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer lands a great operatic part by working hard for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges ROLE plus GOTIT; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's tragic 1851 work about a hunchbacked court jester is one of the best-loved operas.

clue.text: Get it horizontal? Not quite, perhaps

definitions.text: Get it horizontal? Not quite, perhaps

parts.words: Get it horizontal? Not quite, perhaps
parts.note: the phrase means to make something flat; read the other way it describes something not quite flat, i.e. off-true

explanation.surface: A carpenter wonders whether a shelf is truly flat or slightly askew.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb it means make flat or stabilise; taken as an adjective plus 'off', it means not quite flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatten out or stabilise is to bring to a flat state; something slightly out of true is not quite flat.

clue.text: Intoned a formula to be consecrated

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a formula is a set arrangement, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A priest chants a set form of words so that someone may be blessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formula' rearranges INTONED into NOINTED, placed after the A; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be made holy by ritual application of oil is to be sanctified.

clue.text: Replies to all four points in a royal society brief

indicators.note: in means the compass letters sit inside the other letters

parts.note: RS is the abbreviation for the Royal Society, Britain's national science academy
the four compass points are north, south, west and east

explanation.surface: Responses addressed to every item on a short Royal Society agenda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the compass letters as sitting inside the others; 'to' is a link. The Royal Society is Britain's national science academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Responses given to questions or letters are what this word names.

clue.text: Tennis player who gained silver when not quite six

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: not quite means the final letter is dropped from the word six

explanation.surface: A tennis star took a silver medal at a time when he was nearly six.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' cuts the last letter from 'six', leaving SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre is an American former world number one who won eight Grand Slam singles titles.

clue.text: Huge men, semi-dressed…

indicators.note: dressed means the letters are prepared and arranged afresh, as food or a shop window is dressed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Big men who are only half wearing their clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed' rearranges MEN plus SEMI. The dots lead into the next clue's 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enormous or vast in size is very large.

clue.text: Sews in a way which is irritating

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
something that itches is irritating the skin

explanation.surface: Someone sews in a manner others find annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here; 'a way' gives ST, the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To join fabric with needle and thread is to sew.

clue.text: …about to steal fruit

parts.note: about gives CA
to rob means to steal

explanation.surface: Huge men are on the point of stealing some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots continue the previous clue's picture. C stands for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: The pod of a Mediterranean tree, eaten as a sweet chocolate substitute.

clue.text: Garlic, onion, leek — everything one has hesitation to order

parts.note: all means everything
I is the Roman numeral for one
um is a sound made in hesitation

explanation.surface: A cook hesitates over buying every kind of onion family vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'to order' are links; the definition is by example, three members of the genus.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical genus that includes these pungent bulbs and their relatives.

clue.text: Oriental porcelain collected by dim aristocrats

indicators.note: collected by means the letters are held within the run of words dim aristocrats

explanation.surface: Dull-witted nobles collect fine Japanese ceramics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected by' points to letters held in 'dIM ARIstocrats'.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of Japanese export ware named after the port it was shipped from.

clue.text: Greek goddess is subject of woman's article

parts.note: her is the possessive of a woman
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A goddess is the topic of a magazine piece written about a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is subject of' is a link; 'article' is the grammatical word 'a', not a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen of the Olympian deities, wife of Zeus.

clue.text: Sheer chaos in Surrey

indicators.note: chaos means the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Total disorder breaks out in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaos' rearranges SHEER. Surrey is a county south-west of London; the answer is a commuter town there.
explanation.definitionFit: A town south-west of London lies within that county.

clue.text: Practise too hard, concerning coaches

parts.note: over means concerning, as in 'a row over money'
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: An athlete trains too much, prompting a word about the coaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coaches' looks like buses or trainers; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise to excess is to overdo one's preparation.

clue.text: You big ox, take cover — they'll kill you for this!

parts.note: a buffalo is a large wild ox
to hide is to take cover

explanation.surface: A warning to a buffalo to hide from hunters who want its skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You' is a link: the clue addresses the animal. 'cover' does double duty in the surface, as shelter and as a skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunters slaughtered the great bison of the American plains for its skin, as the clue warns the animal.
